headline: Ross Smith knocked out of Grand Slam despite beating Clemens
standfirst: Smith won 5-4 in Group O but missed the margin he needed, while Beau Greaves also went out after beating Niels Zonneveld.
body: Ross Smith's Grand Slam of Darts ended on Sunday night even though he beat Gabriel Clemens 5-4 in Group O, because he needed to win by at least 5-3 to keep his hopes alive.

Having lost to Rusty-Jake Rodriguez on the opening night, the reigning European champion and World Series Finals winner had to win the match by two legs. He had darts at a double to complete a 5-3 win, but missed them, and Clemens took the next leg to level at four apiece. Smith did claim the decider, but the narrow scoreline was not enough. Clemens still has a route through, needing to beat Rodriguez by 5-3 or better on Tuesday.

Beau Greaves also left the tournament. She beat Niels Zonneveld 5-3 in Group A, but the win was not enough to put her in contention for the group. Zonneveld still has a chance of reaching the last 16, though he will need to beat Luke Littler heavily on Monday.

Elsewhere, Ricky Evans survived match darts to beat Cam Crabtree 5-4 in Group K and now plays James Wade for a place in the second round. Henry Coates followed his narrow debut defeat to Michael van Gerwen with a final-leg win over Jeffrey de Graaf, leaving Group L open ahead of de Graaf's meeting with van Gerwen.

Martin Schindler beat Jan Schmidt 5-0 to set up a Group N decider against Chris Dobey on Tuesday. Paolo Nebrida beat Joe Cullen 5-2 and faces Luke Humphries in Group I, Bradley Brooks beat Carl Sneyd 5-3 and meets Gian van Veen in Group M, and Sebastian Bialecki edged Joe Hunt 5-4 to set up a last-16 decider with Gerwyn Price.
